Look up the validation file format, execution rules and reference matching behavior here.

## Validation files

Its validation files describe the process, structure, generated checks, and business rules:

| File                               | Purpose                        |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `survey-validation.yaml`           | Complete execution process     |
| `survey-structure-validation.yaml` | Sheet order and dimensions     |
| `survey-generated-validation.yaml` | Explicit generated field rules |
| `survey-business-validation.yaml`  | Handwritten callback rules     |

```yaml
rulesets:
  structure: survey-structure-validation.yaml
  content:
  - survey-generated-validation.yaml
  - survey-business-validation.yaml
```

All structural checks finish first. Errors or unfinished structural checks block the entire content ruleset.

Content merges generated checks followed by business checks. Only structure gates execution.

The process receives the authoritative form explicitly. Its listed files supply the two ordered rulesets.

Generated rules are written one per line, using the value shortcut whenever possible.

A scalar or sequence is shorthand for `{value: ...}`. Both forms are accepted; severity defaults to error.

```yaml
rules:
  field/Observations.count/mandatory: true
  field/Observations.count/type: integer
  field/Observations.count/minimum: 0
  field/Observations.unit/enum: [cm, m]
  field/Observations.station/reference: {value: stations, severity: warning}
```

Use a mapping when adding properties such as `severity`. Quote strings that YAML could read as numbers or booleans.

Business rules accept the same shortcut: `business/check_total: 1000` passes `config$rule$value = 1000`.

A mapping-valued parameter needs `{value: {key: data}}`; `{}` still means a rule without parameters.

The ID identifies the field and check. Edit the form, then regenerate; stale rules fail to load.

## Custom rules

Rule IDs use `namespace/[field/]callback`. The optional field must exist in the form.

Callbacks are supplied explicitly; YAML never loads R code. Severity defaults to `error`, description to the rule ID.

Additional rule properties reach the callback through `config$rule`.

A structure file may also contain custom rules. They run before content, using the same callback format.

## Results and execution

- `result$findings` records validation findings and their physical locations.
- `result$execution` records check completion, including failures and missing prerequisites.
- `result$complete` indicates whether validation finished.
- Accept data only when `result$complete` and `isTRUE(result$valid)` are both true.

Structural errors or unfinished structural checks block all content checks.

Content checks continue after findings or execution failures; business checks follow generated field checks.

## Alternate reference codes

Reference snapshots may supply explicit aliases alongside canonical values:

```r
references <- list(units = list(values = c("cm", "kg"), aliases = c(CM = "cm")))
```

Membership accepts canonical codes or alias names. Comparisons remain exact and case-sensitive.

Alias targets must exist in `values`; malformed mappings fail execution. Missing snapshots remain incomplete.

Submitted values are never rewritten. Duplicate aliases are allowed: this checks membership, not unique identity.

Accepted keys are cached per validation, or shared across submissions with `prepare_validation_references()`.

The caller supplies all mappings; no data is fetched.

## Registry name matching

Prepare a lookup once from supplied registry values, then reuse it across submissions:

```r
index <- registry_index(c("MARTIN Emile", "Jane Smith"), matching = "name",
  aliases = c("J. Smith" = "Jane Smith"))
registry_match_counts(index, c("Emile Martin", "J. Smith", "Unknown"))
# 1 1 0
```

Lookup tries exact values, explicit aliases, then normalized names. Exactly one registry row must match.

Name keys ignore case, accents, selected punctuation and word order; this is not fuzzy matching.

Exact duplicates and normalized collisions remain ambiguous. Missing alias targets remain unmatched.

Alias chains are supported; cycles fail preparation. Input values and duplicate registry rows are preserved.

`matching = "exact"` is the default. Name matching and aliases require string fields.

The caller chooses matching options and supplies snapshots; these helpers load no files or databases.
